summary: Root cause identified with medium confidence: config change cfg-2207, applied by infra-automation at 09:52Z, cut portfolio-service's Hikari datasource pool from 50 to 5 connections, exhausting the pool at normal concurrency (~12 concurrent connections) and stalling /v1/portfolio/*, which the api-gateway surfaced as upstream-timeout 504s. The reviewed analysis ranks H1 at 0.72 (locked, medium) and clearly ahead of all alternatives, each of which is positively contradicted: the gateway envoy/HTTP-2 upgrade (H2, dep-5220 at 08:00Z) precedes onset by ~1h51m and its expected HTTP/2 reset/protocol error signature is absent; the shared ledger-db stall (H3) is falsified by flat DB cpu/slow_queries, connections_active falling 62→55, and all three other ledger-db consumers flat; the redis branch of H3 is falsified by flat hit_ratio/evictions and flat redis consumers; and load-driven saturation (H4) is refuted by flat request rate ~566 req/s. The positive signature is portfolio-only and internal — Hikari "total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43" from 09:53:19Z with db_pool_in_use pinned at exactly 5.0 — and cfg-2207 is the only change whose timestamp lands inside the 09:51–09:53Z onset window. Residual confidence limit: cfg-2207 is recorded at minute granularity with no accompanying restart/rollout event, so the exact activation second is unobservable and the tight 1-minute alignment with onset is correlation rather than a proven sequence.

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2207 cut portfolio-service datasource pool 50→5, exhausting Hikari and stalling /v1/portfolio/*
ranked_hypotheses.statement: infra-automation applied cfg-2207 at 09:52Z, shrinking portfolio-service's Hikari datasource max pool from 50 to 5 ('cost-optimisation profile small'). At normal concurrency (~12 in-use connections pre-change) the 5-connection cap is insufficient; requests queue on the pool, exhaust the 3s acquisition timeout, and portfolio-service latency/error rate spike. The gateway converts the resulting slow upstream calls into 504s on /v1/portfolio/*. Ledger-db (flat cpu ~30%, slow_queries ~1/min, connections_active FALLING 62→55, all three other ledger-db consumers flat) and redis-cache (hit_ratio flat ~96%, evictions flat ~3/min, both redis consumers flat) are now both shown healthy at onset, leaving the 50→5 pool cut as the only change on the affected path. Residual confidence limit: the exact second the pool change became effective is not observable (minute-granularity, no restart), so the 1-minute alignment with onset is correlation rather than a proven sequence.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2207 applies db.pool.max_size 50->5 to portfolio-service at 09:52:00Z via infra-automation cost-optimisation profile; it is the only change on the portfolio path and the only change in the 09:00-10:30Z all-service sweep
The new 5-connection cap is immediately exhausted: db_pool_in_use drops from ~12 and pins to exactly 5.0 from 09:55Z onward
Hikari logs show pool exhaustion from 09:53:19Z: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (28x) and 'total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43' (39x, 25-57 waiters)
Pool starvation raises portfolio-service p99 from 176ms to ~4.2s and error rate from 0.18% to 22.36% with matching onset

Shared dependencies are healthy, so the stall is not a DB/cache connection-hold: ledger-db cpu ~30% and slow_queries ~1/min flat, connections_active fell 62->55, other ledger-db consumers (order/auth/payment) flat; redis-cache hit_ratio ~96% and evictions ~3/min flat, its consumers (market-data-service/auth-service) flat

Gateway upstream calls to portfolio-service exceed the gateway timeout, producing 'upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504' (252/255 WARN entries, the earliest at 09:53:53Z)
Gateway p99 jumps from ~200ms to 4.3s and 5xx from 0.2% to 7.2% at the same onset
Timing aligns: cfg-2207 at 09:52:00Z falls inside the 09:51-09:53 gateway onset window and ~2 min before the earliest 504 at 09:53:53Z, whereas dep-5220 is ~1h51m earlier
Precedent match: HIST-115 is a datasource pool overridden by a wrong environment profile with identical 'connection is not available / pool exhausted' symptoms (config_change)

assumptions: MAJOR UNRESOLVED (permanent confidence limit): the config change actually took effect and the cap became 5 at ~09:52Z. No sub-minute activation timestamp or restart/rollout event exists (F19,F20,F21), so the 1-minute alignment with onset is correlation, not a proven sequence; the change might have applied at a different second or required a restart.

ranked_hypotheses.title: dep-5220 gateway envoy 1.30 / HTTP/2-to-upstreams upgrade throttled upstream concurrency, stalling portfolio calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The api-gateway deploy dep-5220 (08:00Z, envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol switched to h2 for portfolio-service and order-service) changed HTTP/2 concurrency semantics (max concurrent streams), capping in-flight upstream requests so calls to portfolio-service queue/reset at the gateway, inflating gateway p99 and producing 504s. Reporter's suspicion, repeating HIST-116. The decisive mechanism hop remains unevidenced, and the observed log signature (clean upstream timeouts, no stream resets/protocol errors) contradicts the HIST-116 mechanism; also, a gateway-side throttle cannot explain Hikari pool exhaustion arising inside portfolio-service itself.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5220 deployed to api-gateway at 08:00Z, enabling HTTP/2 to upstreams for portfolio-service (envoy 1.29->1.30), still live and not rolled back
The envoy HTTP/2 concurrency default reduces effective upstream concurrency, queueing portfolio requests at the gateway
Gateway p99 rises to ~4.3s and 5xx to 7.2%, producing 504s on /v1/portfolio/*
Upstream calls time out with 'upstream timeout portfolio-service ... -> 504' in gateway WARN logs

assumptions: UNVERIFIED mechanism: no config diff confirming envoy 1.30 HTTP/2 max-concurrent-streams semantics was retrievable (gap), so this is retained low-rank rather than fully falsified.

FAILED as written: gateway error logs show only clean 'upstream timeout' entries with NO HTTP/2 stream/reset or protocol errors, whereas HIST-116 was defined by HTTP/2 max-concurrent-streams defects producing resets.
A gateway-side concurrency limit would not push portfolio-service into Hikari pool exhaustion inside portfolio-service itself, downstream of any gateway throttle (F5/F6).
Timing: deploy precedes onset by ~1h51m with no intermediate symptoms, which weakens this cause (F14).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared dependency ledger-db (or redis-cache) degraded, stalling portfolio-service and cascading to the gateway
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared single-point-of-failure on the /v1/portfolio/* path — ledger-db (postgres, also used by order-service, auth-service, payment-service) or redis-cache (also used by auth-service, market-data-service) — degraded at ~09:52Z. portfolio-service threads block waiting on the DB/cache, holding pool connections to the cap, the pool reports 'exhausted', and the gateway surfaces 504s. Now positively falsified for both branches: ledger-db server-side load was flat (cpu ~30%, slow_queries ~1/min), connections_active FELL rather than rose (62->55), and no other ledger-db consumer degraded; redis-cache proxies are flat (hit_ratio ~96%, evictions ~3/min) and both redis consumers (market-data-service, auth-service) show no elevation.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db and redis-cache are shared=true single points of failure on the portfolio path
ledger-db or redis-cache degraded (failover / IOPS throttle / slow queries) around onset, holding portfolio-service connections
Held connections make the pool look exhausted; portfolio-service p99 rises to ~4.2s and errors to 22.36%
Gateway converts the slow upstream calls into 504s on /v1/portfolio/*

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Both branches are contradicted. ledger-db: flat cpu (~30%) and slow_queries (~1/min), connections_active FELL 62->55 (a holding stall would show pile-up), and all three other ledger-db consumers (order/auth/payment) are flat at onset (F23,F24,F25,F27). redis-cache: proxies flat (hit_ratio ~96%, evictions ~3/min) and both redis consumers (market-data-service, auth-service) flat at onset (F29-F33). The only service that stalls is portfolio-service, whose pool was cut to 5 — inconsistent with a shared-component cause.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Traffic/capacity saturation on the portfolio path with no faulty change (coincidence with gateway upgrade)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A load spike or resource saturation (CPU/memory/connection pool) on the portfolio path drove p99 and 504s, with the gateway upgrade and the pool cut both temporal coincidences. Positively refuted: portfolio-service request_rate was flat at ~566 req/s across the entire window including onset, so there was no traffic increase to trigger saturation; and two independent changes (cfg-2207, dep-5220) inside/around the onset window make coincidence implausible.

causal_chain.claim: A sudden load spike hits the portfolio endpoint around 09:52Z
portfolio-service saturates its datasource pool (pinned at 5) and reports acquisition timeouts
Latency/errors cascade to api-gateway as 504s

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Directly refuted by F26: portfolio-service request_rate was flat at ~566 req/s (mean 566.13, min 526.33, max 599.69) across the entire window including onset — there was no traffic increase to drive saturation. The pool being pinned at exactly the 5-connection cap coinciding with the 09:52Z pool cut also argues against coincidence (F13/F14).

facts.statement: api-gateway p99 latency was flat ~200-215ms through 09:51Z, then jumped to 4323ms in the 09:53Z bucket; onset lies between 09:51 and 09:53Z.
api-gateway 5xx error rate rose from ~0.2% baseline to 7.2%+ from the 09:50Z/09:55Z buckets, matching the 504 storm.

The earliest 504 on /v1/portfolio/* in gateway WARN logs is 09:53:53Z ('upstream timeout portfolio-service GET /v1/portfolio/holdings -> 504'); this pattern accounts for 252 of 255 WARN entries, and no DNS or TLS/HTTP2 protocol errors appear.
portfolio-service shows the same onset: p99 rose from 176.42ms (09:45Z) to 1865.15ms avg/max 4546.3ms (09:50Z) and ~4.2s thereafter, with error rate rising from 0.18% to 22.36%.

portfolio-service logs are dominated by Hikari JDBC pool exhaustion beginning 09:53:19Z: 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' (28 occurrences) and 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)' (39 occurrences), with 25-57 waiters.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was steady ~12 connections until 09:45Z, then dropped at 09:50Z (avg 9.17, max 12.22) and from 09:55Z is pinned flat at exactly 5.0 (max 5), consistent with saturation at a 5-connection cap.

Only one deployment occurred across all services in 2026-03-10T00:00Z-11:59Z: dep-5220 on api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00:00Z ('Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams', envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service), still live with rolled_back_at=null.

Two config changes occurred in the window, neither on api-gateway: cfg-2199 order-service log.sampling_rate 0.1->0.2 at 07:00Z (logging only), and cfg-2207 portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 09:52:00Z by 'infra-automation' ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource').

The /v1/portfolio/* dependency path is api-gateway -> portfolio-service -> {ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache)}; ledger-db and redis-cache are shared single points of failure, ledger-db also serving order-service, auth-service and payment-service, and redis-cache also serving auth-service and market-data-service.

portfolio-service had no deployments between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-10T00:00Z, and api-gateway had no config changes in 2026-03-01T00:00Z-11:59Z: on the reported path the only code change is dep-5220 and the only config change is cfg-2207.
In a fine-grained 09:00-10:30Z window across all services there is exactly one config change, cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 09:52:00Z), and zero deployments in 09:00-11:59Z.

No config changes outside cfg-2207 and the benign order-service log sampling (cfg-2199, 07:00Z) were found; a 09:00-10:30Z all-service sweep returned only cfg-2207, so no change touched shared components ledger-db or redis-cache in this window.

Historical precedent HIST-115 (2025-09-25, order-service) exactly matches the cfg-2207 pattern: symptoms 'connection is not available / request timed out / pool exhausted', root cause 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', category config_change; HIST-116 is the competing gateway-envoy/HTTP2 precedent.
cfg-2207 is recorded at minute granularity only (changed_at '2026-03-10T09:52:00Z'); no sub-minute activation/apply timestamp is exposed.

No restart/rollout event accompanies cfg-2207: portfolio-service deployments for 2026-03-10T00:00Z-11:59Z returned count 0, and an all-services deployment query for 09:40Z-11:59Z also returned count 0.

A tight 6-minute deployment sweep (09:50Z-09:56Z, all services) returned zero deployments, and a portfolio-service-scoped config sweep (09:45Z-10:00Z) returned only cfg-2207; no infra-automation config-apply deployment or restart event appears at/just after 09:52Z.

ledger-db server-side load was flat through and after onset: cpu_pct mean 30.03% (range 26.26-32.15) and slow_queries_per_min flat ~1/min; no DB-side latency or slow-query spike coincides with the 09:52-09:53Z onset.
ledger-db connections_active FELL rather than climbed after onset, roughly 62 -> 55 (57.17 avg at 09:50Z, 54.72 avg at 09:55Z); a degraded/holding DB would show connection pile-up, not a drop.

None of the other ledger-db consumers show latency elevation around the window: order-service p99 flat ~149ms, auth-service ~90ms, payment-service ~317ms; a shared ledger-db stall would have degraded these too.
portfolio-service request_rate was flat at ~566 req/s across the whole window including onset (mean 566.13, min 526.33, max 599.69), ruling out a load-driven explanation for the portfolio-only stall.
redis-cache hit_ratio_pct was flat/normal across 09:45-10:00Z including onset (min 94.15, max 97.37, mean 96.03, values 95.72 at 09:52Z and 95.69 at 09:53Z) with no dip.
redis-cache evictions_per_min stayed low and normal through onset (09:52Z avg 5.09, 09:53Z avg 3.61; window min 1.42, max 5.11, mean 3.28 keys/min), with no eviction storm or memory-pressure spike.
market-data-service (a redis-cache consumer) was flat across 09:45-10:00Z: latency_p99_ms 37.01-42.61ms (09:53Z 41.76) and error_rate 0.10-0.31% (mean 0.20).
auth-service (the other redis-cache consumer) was flat across 09:45-10:00Z: latency_p99_ms 85.66-95.51ms and error_rate 0.11-0.30% (mean 0.20).

assumptions: The config change cfg-2207 actually took effect and the pool cap became 5 at ~09:52Z. No sub-minute activation timestamp or restart/rollout event exists (F19, F20, F21), so the 1-minute alignment with onset is a tight correlation, not a proven sequence; the change might have applied at a different second or required a restart to take effect.
The pre-change concurrency baseline of ~12 in-use connections (and thus that a 5-connection cap is insufficient) is taken from the team's verified finding F6 rather than an independent re-query.
The reviewed hypothesis ranking and confidences (H1 = 0.72 medium, H2 = 0.08, H3 = 0.02 rejected, H4 = 0.02 rejected) are fixed by the reviewed analysis and are not re-derived in this report.

ledger-db and redis-cache health is inferred from the available proxy signals (DB cpu/slow_queries/connections_active; redis hit_ratio/evictions plus consumer health), since neither exposes a direct query-latency metric (F22, F28).

The absence of HTTP/2 stream/reset or protocol errors in gateway WARN logs (F3) is representative of the gateway error population for the incident window, so the HIST-116 style mechanism is not occurring.
Traffic and workload conditions in the 09:45-10:00Z window on the portfolio path are typical (no unmeasured surge), based on flat request_rate (F26).

timeline.event: Benign config change cfg-2199 applied to order-service (log.sampling_rate 0.1->0.2); logging only, not on the gateway path.

Deployment dep-5220 goes live on api-gateway v9.3.0 ('Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams', envoy 1.29->1.30, upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service). It remains live (rolled_back_at=null).
Last measured healthy interval on the path: gateway p99 flat ~200-215ms, portfolio-service p99 176.42ms, db_pool_in_use ~12 connections, ledger-db connections_active ~61-63, redis hit_ratio ~96%.

Config change cfg-2207 applied by infra-automation: portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource'). It is the only change in the 09:00-10:30Z all-service sweep and lands inside the onset window. No accompanying restart or rollout event is recorded.

Gateway p99 begins rising (5-min bucket avg 1849.99ms, max 4418.76ms); portfolio-service p99 rises to 1865.15ms avg; db_pool_in_use drops to avg 9.17/max 12.22; ledger-db connections_active begins falling (57.17 avg); no elevation in order/auth/payment or in redis signals.

Gateway p99 ~4323ms in the 09:53Z bucket; 5xx error rate rises to 7.2%+; gateway begins emitting upstream-timeout 504s on /v1/portfolio/*, with the earliest at 09:53:53Z; portfolio-service Hikari pool exhaustion begins at 09:53:19Z ('total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43').

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use pinned flat at exactly 5.0 (max 5); portfolio-service error rate at 22.36%; redis hit_ratio and evictions and both redis consumers remain flat; order/auth/payment latency remain flat.
Incident INC-002 (SEV-2) reported: portfolio page timing out, gateway p99 > 4s, 504s on /v1/portfolio/*; reporter suspects the morning gateway upgrade.
ledger-db connections_active remains low (54.7) confirming no DB-side connection pile-up; ledger-db cpu and slow_queries remain flat.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately revert config change cfg-2207: restore portfolio-service db.pool.max_size from 5 back to 50 (re-apply the normal, non-'small' datasource profile) and confirm the change is applied to the running portfolio-service instances.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 is the only change on the affected path and its 09:52Z timestamp lands inside the 09:51-09:53Z onset window; the pool-exhaustion signature (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43) and db_pool_in_use pinned at exactly 5.0 are the direct consequence of a 10x undersized pool at normal ~12-connection concurrency (F5, F6, F8, F13, F14).

recommended_actions.action: While the revert is applied, verify recovery: watch portfolio-service Hikari 'waiting' count, db_pool_in_use rising above 5, portfolio-service p99/error rate, and gateway p99 and 504 rate over the next 10-15 minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the exact signals that degraded at onset, so their normalization confirms the causal chain rather than an unrelated coincidence (F1, F2, F4, F5, F6).

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back api-gateway dep-5220 as the first action; if the pool revert does not restore service, then evaluate rolling back dep-5220 (envoy 1.29 / HTTP2-to-upstreams) as a secondary mitigation.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 has an unevidenced mechanism hop, precedes onset by ~1h51m with no intermediate symptoms, and F3 shows clean upstream timeouts with no HTTP/2 stream/reset or protocol errors, contradicting the HIST-116 signature (F3, F7, F14, F18).

recommended_actions.action: Guard the cost-optimisation profile automation: require the 'small' datasource profile to be applied only after comparing it against measured peak concurrent pool usage for the service, and block any profile that sets db.pool.max_size below last-30-day peak concurrent connections.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-115 is the identical precedent (datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile causing pool exhaustion), and F6 shows a steady ~12-connection working set that a 5-connection cap could never serve (F6, F18).

recommended_actions.action: Add pool-saturation alerting: alert on Hikari pending/waiting threads > 0 or acquisition-timeout errors, and on db_pool_in_use pinned at the configured max for more than a few minutes, with the configured pool cap exported as a metric so cap reductions are visible.
recommended_actions.rationale: Detection currently relied on downstream gateway 504s; the decisive in-service signature ('could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms', 'total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43') was only visible in logs, and the pool cap itself was not observable before the change (F5, F6, F19).

recommended_actions.action: Emit a sub-minute activation/effectivity timestamp (and restart/rollout linkage) for config changes such as cfg-2207 so future incidents can prove or disprove the exact activation second.
recommended_actions.rationale: The permanent confidence limit on this conclusion is that cfg-2207 is minute-granularity only with no restart event, leaving the 1-minute alignment with onset as correlation rather than a proven sequence (F19, F20, F21).

data_gaps: No sub-minute activation timestamp or restart/rollout event exists for cfg-2207 (minute-granularity change record; zero deployments for portfolio-service in the window), so the exact second the 5-connection pool became active is unobservable and the 1-minute alignment with onset remains correlation. This is a permanent data-source limit, not a query that can be retried.

Downstream database query latency / connection checkout time could not be measured: ledger-db exposes only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms and slow_queries_per_min, so its 'normal' verdict rests on proxy signals rather than measured query latency.
portfolio-service cpu_pct, memory_pct and restart history were never retrieved (budget_exhausted), so it cannot be shown whether resource pressure or a restart preceded the pool exhaustion.

redis-cache connected_clients, memory_pct and cpu_pct were not retrieved (budget_exhausted), and redis-cache exposes no direct latency or error-rate metric, so redis client pile-up and memory pressure are unverified; the redis 'healthy' verdict rests on hit_ratio/evictions plus consumer health.
order-service, auth-service and payment-service error rates were not fetched (only latency_p99_ms), so a latent error-only elevation in other ledger-db consumers would not have been seen.

No metric time series were available for api-gateway, portfolio-service, ledger-db or redis-cache in the dependency-tool agent's toolset, so which signal fired first could not be confirmed from a single consistent source.

Market-data-service and exchange-gateway telemetry (beyond latency/error for market-data-service) was not retrieved, so a change or degradation on a leaf dependency outside the queried ranges cannot be fully excluded.

The full configuration diff / HTTP2 max-concurrent-streams settings for the HIST-116 envoy precedent were not retrievable, so it cannot be stated whether dep-5220 repeats that specific configuration defect (H2 is rebutted on mechanism and timing, not on a retrieved config diff).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that portfolio-service's datasource pool cap was NOT actually 5 during the incident (e.g. cfg-2207 failed to apply, was superseded, or required a restart that never occurred) would break H1's first causal hop and force re-ranking.
Any observed degradation of another ledger-db consumer (order-service, auth-service, payment-service) in latency or error rate at 09:52-09:53Z would revive the shared-DB stall hypothesis (H3).
Evidence of redis-cache connection pile-up, memory pressure, restart/failover, or a latency spike at onset (connected_clients rising sharply, memory_pct spiking) would revive H3's redis branch.
Hikari exhaustion appearing with a pool cap larger than the concurrency demand (e.g. waiting threads at a cap of 50) would indicate a different mechanism than an undersized pool.
HTTP/2 stream resets, protocol errors, or max-concurrent-streams throttling at the gateway coinciding with onset would support H2 (dep-5220) over H1.
A measured ledger-db query latency or checkout-time spike at 09:52-09:53Z (not readable from current metrics) would support a shared-DB holding stall over the pool-cap explanation.

Discovery of another change on the /v1/portfolio/* path — e.g. a market-data-service or redis-cache change outside the queried window/scope — would introduce an alternative origin not covered by the current ranking.

findings.statement: Dependency map for the /v1/portfolio/* path: api-gateway -> portfolio-service (http); portfolio-service -> ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache); market-data-service -> redis-cache and exchange-gateway. Shared components (single points of failure) on this path are ledger-db (postgres, shared=true) and redis-cache (redis, shared=true); ledger-db is also used by order-service, auth-service and payment-service, and redis-cache by auth-service and market-data-service.

portfolio-service itself had NO deployments between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-10T00:00Z (count 0), and api-gateway had NO config changes 2026-03-01T00:00Z–11:59Z (count 0) — so on the reported path the only code change is the gateway dep-5220 and the only config change is cfg-2207 on portfolio-service.

Historical precedents for this exact signature (p99/504 on portfolio/gateway): HIST-116 (2025-12-18) 'HTTP/2 resets after gateway envoy upgrade' — root cause 'Envoy upgrade changed HTTP/2 max concurrent streams default', resolution rolled back gateway; HIST-102 (2025-09-02) 'Portfolio timeouts during ledger-db failover' — shared DB failure, 504 at gateway; HIST-115 (2025-09-25) order-service pool exhausted from a wrong environment profile (config_change). All are leads only — same symptoms, different established causes.

findings.statement: Two changes straddle the 10:05Z report time and pull in opposite directions: the gateway HTTP/2 change deployed 08:00Z (envoy default concurrency semantics, cf. HIST-116) and the portfolio db pool cut 50->5 applied 09:52Z, only 13 minutes before the report. The pool cut is on the exact /v1/portfolio/* path and matches the HIST-115 pattern (datasource pool reduced by a profile) while the deploy matches HIST-116. Data here does not discriminate between them.

In a fine-grained window (09:00–10:30Z) across ALL services there is exactly one config change: cfg-2207 portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z by 'infra-automation' ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource') — and zero deployments in 09:00–11:59Z, confirming the 08:00Z gateway deploy is the only earlier change.

cfg-2207's changed_at (09:52:00Z) falls inside the T1-derived onset window for api-gateway p99 (between 09:51 and 09:53Z) and precedes the earliest portfolio 504 (09:53:53Z per T1/F3) by ~2 minutes, whereas dep-5220 deployed at 08:00:00Z, ~1h51m earlier.

dep-5220 on api-gateway (v9.3.0, 08:00Z, 'envoy 1.29 -> 1.30', 'upstream protocol h2 for portfolio-service and order-service') is the sole deployment in the window and is still live with rolled_back_at=null (not rolled back).

No config changes outside cfg-2207 and the benign order-service log sampling (cfg-2199, 07:00Z) were found; a 09:00Z–10:30Z all-service sweep returned only cfg-2207, so no change touched the shared components ledger-db or redis-cache in this window.

The /v1/portfolio/* dependency map confirms api-gateway -> portfolio-service -> {ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache)}; ledger-db and redis-cache are shared=true single points of failure, and the only change on this path is cfg-2207 on portfolio-service itself.

Historical precedent HIST-115 (2025-09-25, order-service) exactly matches the cfg-2207 pattern: symptoms 'connection is not available / request timed out / pool exhausted', root cause 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', category config_change; HIST-116 (2025-12-18) is the competing gateway-envoy/HTTP2 precedent (match_score 5 vs 3 for the pool-search and portfolio-search respectively).

findings.statement: cfg-2207 is recorded at minute granularity only: changed_at '2026-03-10T09:52:00Z', portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50->5, author 'infra-automation', description 'Apply cost-optimisation profile small to service datasource'. No sub-minute activation/apply timestamp is exposed by this tool, so no exact activation second can be derived here.

No restart/rollout event accompanies cfg-2207: get_deployments for portfolio-service over 2026-03-10T00:00Z–11:59Z returned count 0, and an all-services deployment query for 09:40Z–11:59Z also returned count 0. There is no recorded pod restart, rolling update or rollout event for portfolio-service at or just after 09:52Z.

A tight 6-minute deployment sweep (09:50Z–09:56Z, all services) returned zero deployments, and a portfolio-service-scoped config sweep (09:45Z–10:00Z) returned only cfg-2207. No infra-automation config-apply deployment or restart event appears at/just after 09:52Z in either feed.

ledger-db exposes no direct query-latency or checkout/connection-hold metric; its available_metrics are only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min, so the requested DB query latency/checkout time cannot be read directly.

ledger-db server-side load was flat through and after onset: cpu_pct mean 30.03% (range 26.26-32.15) with 09:49Z avg 29.96/max 31.37 and 09:56Z avg 30.41/max 32.15, and slow_queries_per_min flat ~1/min (09:45Z avg 1.16, 09:50Z avg 0.83, 09:55Z avg 1.03, 10:00Z avg 1.13). No DB-side latency or slow-query spike coincides with the 09:52-09:53Z onset.

ledger-db connections_active FELL rather than climbed after onset: ~61-63 from 09:00-09:45Z, then 57.17 avg (09:50Z), 54.72 avg (09:55Z), 55.49 (10:00Z), 54.7 (10:15Z) -- i.e. roughly 62 -> 55. A degraded/holding DB would show connection pile-up, not a drop, so no DB-side connection-hold stall is visible.

None of the other ledger-db consumers show any latency/error elevation around the window. order-service latency_p99_ms is flat: 09:51Z avg 147.93, 09:54Z 149.25, 09:57Z 153.58, 10:00Z 146.84 (mean 149.06, over the whole span). auth-service p99 flat: 09:51Z 90.79, 09:54Z 89.84, 09:57Z 89.46 (mean 90.24). payment-service p99 flat: 09:51Z 317.14, 09:54Z 327.52, 09:57Z 315.85 (mean 317.48). A shared ledger-db stall (H3) would have degraded these too.

portfolio-service request_rate was flat at ~566 req/s across the whole window including onset: 09:51Z avg 567.64/max 585.08, 09:54Z avg 556.96/max 577.16, 09:57Z avg 559.07, 10:00Z 561.85 (mean 566.13, min 526.33, max 599.69). No traffic spike at 09:52-09:53Z, which rules out a load-driven (H4) explanation for the portfolio-only stall.

Discriminator result: the shared dependency ledger-db shows no server-side degradation (flat cpu ~30%, flat ~1 slow query/min, no connection build-up) and no other consumer degrades in 09:45-10:00Z, while the only service that stalls is portfolio-service -- the one whose datasource pool was cut 50->5 at 09:52Z (cfg-2207) with db_pool_in_use pinned at its 5-connection cap. This pattern matches H1 (portfolio-only undersized pool exhausting at ~12 concurrent callers) and is inconsistent with H3 (shared ledger-db/redis stall, which would degrade order/auth/payment equally).

redis-cache exposes NO direct latency or error-rate metric. Its available_metrics are exactly ['connected_clients','cpu_pct','evictions_per_min','hit_ratio_pct','memory_pct']; queries for latency_p99_ms (tc-039) and error_rate (tc-044) both returned not_found. So redis latency must be inferred from proxy signals: hit_ratio, evictions, connected_clients, memory, cpu.

redis-cache evictions_per_min stayed low and normal through onset: 09:52Z avg 5.09 (max 5.09), 09:53Z avg 3.61, over the window min 1.42, max 5.11, mean 3.28 keys/min. No eviction storm or memory-pressure eviction spike coincides with 09:52-09:53Z.

market-data-service (a redis-cache consumer per the dependency map) was flat across 09:45-10:00Z: latency_p99_ms ranged 37.01-42.61ms (09:52Z 41.24, 09:53Z 41.76, mean 40.16) and error_rate stayed 0.10-0.31% (09:53Z 0.29, mean 0.20) — no degradation at onset.

auth-service (the other redis-cache consumer) was flat across 09:45-10:00Z: latency_p99_ms ranged 85.66-95.51ms (09:52Z 88.19, 09:53Z 95.51, mean 90.24) and error_rate 0.11-0.30% (mean 0.20) — no degradation at onset.

Neither redis-cache consumer (market-data-service, auth-service) shows any latency or error elevation in 09:45-10:00Z, and redis-cache's only readable proxy signals (hit_ratio ~96%, evictions ~3/min) are flat — so the shared redis-cache is not showing degradation at 09:52-09:53Z, which argues against H3's redis-stall branch.
